newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's San Paolo announces share prices.
newsitem.headline: Italy's San Paolo announces share prices.

text.p: Italian bank San Paolo di Torino said on Saturday the final price to the public for its share offer would be 10,435 lire per share and the price for institutional investors would be 10,630 lire per share.

"The offer price...is the lower of the maximum price announced at the start of the OPV (public sale offer) and the official price on...the Italian bourse on...May 23 (10,702 lire per share), minus the 2.5 percent discount to the public," San Paolo said in a statement.
The announcement was made after the board of the bank met on Saturday in Turin.
Analysts' calculations made on Friday after the Milan stock exchange closed had estimated the public offer price would be around 10,434.45 lire per share.

The bank said 120 million shares would be allocated to the public, 20 million of which would go to San Paolo employees at a price of 10,175 lire per share -- "equal to the public share offer price minus a further 2.5 percent discount".

The bank said that because of heavy demand it would not be possible to assign the full amount of the shares requested by the public to all subscribers. Shares would therefore be distributed by resorting to a lottery system.

The statement said the price for istitutional investors "was defined by taking into account the public offer price, the interest (price/amount) expressed by institutional investors, domestic and international market conditions and the demand expressed during the offer".
San Paolo said on Friday its global share offer was more than three times oversubscribed.
The global offer was for 220 million ordinary shares.
The bank said that at the end of the offer period the total demand for the public sale offer and the offer to institutional investors was more than 760 million shares.
The public offer registered applications by more than 400,000 subscribers for more than 460 million shares, including San Paolo employees.
For the institutional offer, there were requests by 400 investors for more than 300 million shares.
